# @amykit/workflow-note-to-plan

The note-to-plan workflow: friction becomes a plan in the repository it is about.

A workflow for [amy](https://github.com/nicolasmelo1/amy): a pure `plan()` that says what
happens next, and a runtime that says how each step is done. The engine drives it without
knowing what any of its states mean.

## Install

```sh
npm install -g @amykit/workflow-note-to-plan
```

Then name it in `~/.amy/config.yaml`:

```yaml
workflows:
  note-to-plan:
    workflow: "@amykit/workflow-note-to-plan"
```

## The lifecycle

| State | Kind |
| :-- | :-- |
| `NOTED` | initial, waiting |
| `DRAFTED` | working |
| `CHECKED` | working |
| `PR_OPEN` | working |
| `DONE` | terminal |
| `DECLINED` | terminal |

It emits `announce`, `check-plan`, `draft-plan` and `open-pull-request`.

## Configuration

```yaml
plugins:
  "@amykit/workflow-note-to-plan":
    defaultBranch: "main"
    policy: {}
    repos: <string[]>
```

| Setting | Type | Required | Default | What it is |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `defaultBranch` | `string` | no | `main` | the branch a plan branch is cut from, which is not always `main` |
| `policy` | `record` | no | `{}` | maxDraftAttempts, maxOpenPlansPerRepo and ceilingBackoffMs. Anything left out keeps its default |
| `repos` | `string[]` | **yes** |  | the repositories a plan may be written into. A note about anything else is handed back to the operator |

Every field is checked at boot against the schema this package declares. A key that is
not one of the above is a refusal naming the plugin and the key, not a setting that
silently never applied.
